security.title: Security Center
security.description: Manage OpenClaw's execution policy and instruction approval allowlist, ensuring Agent operations meet your security requirements.
security.philosophyContent:
### 1. Duty Segregation

• **Instruction Ask (Ask) = Identity Verification / Access Control**
The core is 'Interaction'. It focuses on: **'Do I need to ask the boss (you) about this?'**. If enabled, the Agent must obtain your approval before taking any action.

• **Security Level (Security) = Laboratory Rules / Physical Constraints**
The core is 'Constraint'. It focuses on: **'Within the allowed scope, what dangerous items can it touch?'**. This determines the strength of sandbox isolation and interception during command execution.

---

### 2. Their Relationship

**'Ask is the first line of defense, Security is the ultimate line of defense'**

• **Cross Defense**: Even if you accidentally click 'Allow' in an Ask prompt, if the Security level is set to `full`, the system will still intercept dangerous operations at the low level.

• **Priority**: If the Security level is set to `deny` (Deny All), no more Ask prompts will be triggered because the command is directly intercepted.
security.presetYoloDesc: Fully automated, no questions. Security: None
security.presetCautiousDesc: Cautious mode, confirmation for key commands. Security: Full
security.askOnMissDesc: Ask only if not in allowlist, balanced
security.securityDenyDesc: Block all Shell requests, highest alert
security.askHelpContent:
Determines whether Agent needs your approval before executing a Shell command.

• **Always Ask (on)**: Safest. A confirmation prompt will appear before every command.

• **Ask On Miss (on-miss)**: Balanced. Commands in the allowlist execute automatically, others need confirmation.

• **Ask Off (off)**: Fastest. Agent can execute all commands silently. Ensure you trust the Agent.
security.securityHelpContent:
Determines the defense and restriction strength during command execution.

• **Security Full (full)**: Recommended. Enables sandbox restrictions, prevents access to sensitive system files, and intercepts dangerous operations.

• **Allowlist Mode (allowlist)**: Strict. Only allows execution of commands you have explicitly authorized in the list on the right.

• **Security None (none)**: Developer Mode. Commands execute with your current user permissions without extra protection.

• **Deny All (deny)**: Lockdown. Prohibits all Shell command execution.
security.allowlistHelpContent:
The allowlist grants authorization for specific commands to run automatically without manual confirmation.

• **Matching Patterns**: Supports wildcards. For example, `npm install *` will permit any command starting with npm install, and `git **` will allow all git operations.

• **Exact Match**: If you enter only `ls`, only the bare ls command without arguments will be allowed.

• **Scope**: You can set allowlists for specific Agents or select `* (All Agents)` for global application.

• **Security Tip**: Avoid adding dangerous commands like `sudo *` or `rm *` to the allowlist.
security.noPatterns: No custom allowlist for this agent
security.saveConfirm: Are you sure you want to apply these security changes?
security.advancedHelpContent:
• **Core File**: `exec-approvals.json` is the core configuration file of the OpenClaw permission system and holds the highest decision-making priority.

• **JSON Editing**: By directly editing the JSON, you can manually configure more complex permission rules, such as authorizing specific IPs, nodes, or system calls.

• **Risk Warning**: Incorrect JSON syntax may cause permission verification to fail or prevent the Agent from executing any commands. Please check the structure carefully before saving.

quotes.sub: A contract from the out-of-band, written at every packet drop.
Capturing every tremor on the bit plains.
Hearing a beating heart among the silent racks.
The last tenderness before the system crashes.
Waiting for the lobster's sunset, asking for no return.

login.typewriter: "I've heard people say that if coffee doesn't have a companion, it's not called coffee—it's called bitter water. In this era of polite refusals, the air is filled with the humidity of being alone. But I always feel that even a lobster built of code needs something to rely on. OpenClaw Buddy, it's right there, 0.01 cm away from you. It doesn't speak; it just stays there with you, watching over those little lobsters. I hope one day, you also find that person who makes you no longer need a 'monitoring sentinel'."
